source.practice_formula: (current percent - attribute penalty + effective teacher percent) / 2

mage.strategy: Convert intellectual practices into reliable spell damage first, then keep extending the source prerequisite chain instead of stopping at burning hands. Build shield and stone skin when their exact protection gates become teachable, while retaining the source-defined familiar and cheap travel safety.
mage.practice_policy: Reach evocation magiks 30% for chill touch, then 45% for burning hands. Continue through shocking grasp, lightning bolt, colour spray, fireball, and acid blast only when the live teacher listing and prerequisite graph permit each step; raise protection and armor to the exact shield and stone-skin gates, then preserve practices after executable priorities are exhausted.
automation_gaps: The field controller now summons and orders the source-defined familiar outdoors and maintains every known self-protection spell; higher spell transitions still require live trainer evidence, resource reserves, and target-specific resistance checks.

cleric.strategy: Unlock cause serious for direct damage, then buy efficient self-healing that can extend field segments while preserving a fixed mana reserve; next establish protection and sanctuary before adding passive attacks and shield mitigation.
cleric.practice_policy: Reach healing and harmful magiks 30%, cause light 30%, and cause serious first. Then raise cure light and cure serious to 30%; train protective magiks to 45%, protection to 40%, and sanctuary to 40% when each appears on the live teacher list. The combat controller permits at most two self-heals below 35% health while retaining 30% mana, and protection buffs remain subject to their casting reserve.
automation_gaps: Protection and sanctuary now have source-backed training priorities and use the existing self-buff upkeep; subclass-specific defensive spells remain source-gated by live skill listings.

thief.strategy: Buy passive attack frequency, unlock a high-damage backstab opener and its automatic double-backstab branch, then combine repeatable knife-toss damage with the source-backed third-attack chain before the longer disarm and circle chains.
thief.practice_policy: Raise stealth techniques to 60%, hide to 20%, and sneak to 40%, then learn a functional backstab. Raise thievery skills to 40% and knife toss to 45%, then reach 60% in Armed Combat Knowledge and second attack to unlock third attack. Buy a functional third attack before improving its second-attack gate, third attack, and backstab toward the current trainer caps.
automation_gaps: Backstab and circle depend on maintaining an accessible piercing or stabbing weapon; trip and dirt kick require source-gated control dispatch and transient target-state checks.
source_refs: server/src/fight.c: do_backstab, do_knife_toss, do_circle, do_disarm, multi_hit, and check_dodge

warrior.strategy: Maximize ordinary combat rounds with extra attacks and weapon-hit multipliers, then build grip and disarm so armed opponents lose damage and weapon-dependent control; add headbutt when its source anatomy gate is proven.
warrior.practice_policy: Prioritize second attack and armed combat knowledge 40%, keep raising enhanced damage when the trainer allows it, then raise second attack to 60% and learn third attack before lower-value combat options. Build shield block, defense knowledge, dodge, parry, and grip through the exact disarm gates; use headbutt and kick when their unarmed prerequisites and source anatomy gates are satisfied, with a pounding weapon ready before stun.
automation_gaps: Later attack chains require class-teacher availability and live confirmation at their unlock levels.
source_refs: server/src/fight.c: multi_hit, one_hit, do_headbutt, do_kick, and do_stun

psionic.strategy: Concentrate intellectual practices on the shortest direct-damage chain, then add agitation after its matter-control gate because the same unspent practice pool also increases next-level mana.
psionic.practice_policy: Raise mind thrust to 30%, telepathy disciplines to 45%, and psychic crush next; add matter control and agitation when the trainer exposes them, while deferring alternate disciplines until their combat or sustain lifecycle is implemented.
automation_gaps: Psychic healing still needs a separate sustain policy; known mental defenses and later alternate disciplines remain source-gated.

shifter.strategy: Use normal-form passive attacks, dodge, and recovery for early leveling. Chameleon, hawk, and cat are utility forms; snake is the first form that creates a natural weapon but sits behind a long intellectual-practice chain.
shifter.practice_policy: Spend early physical practices on second attack, dodge, and fast healing. Preserve intellectual practices until a form controller can justify the group forms 40%, chameleon 40%, hawk 32%, cat 40%, and snake path without sacrificing excessive level-up mana.
automation_gaps: The straight-shifter form controller now enters a known snake form, source-ranked output recognizes its source-created fangs, and normal form is restored at the healer; later form selection, live damage calibration, and travel behavior remain. The werewolf controller covers source-created wolf weapons and wolf attacks, while rage and endgame lycanthropy still need dedicated lifecycle policies.
source_refs: server/src/sft.c: do_morph and early form implementations

brawler.strategy: Combine passive extra attacks and enhanced damage with punch, then add headbutt when source anatomy and live combat state make its damage and lag worthwhile.
brawler.practice_policy: Reach combat knowledge 40% and second attack, then pugilism knowledge 40% and one punch lesson. Keep enhanced damage as the main physical target after punch is usable; revisit punch at 51% for second punch, then raise headbutt once its unarmed gate is satisfied.
automation_gaps: Later grappling and control actions need target anatomy, trauma, position, and lag-aware policies.
source_refs: server/src/fight.c: multi_hit, one_hit, do_headbutt, and check_dodge

ranger.strategy: Build passive melee frequency and a source-backed opening bow volley, then extend the defensive chain through grip and disarm to suppress armed opponents.
ranger.practice_policy: Reach armed combat knowledge 20% for second attack. When a source-identified bow is equipped, reach archery knowledge 20% and improve shoot; otherwise preserve those practices. Then raise defense knowledge, dodge, parry, and grip through the exact disarm gates.
automation_gaps: The engine still needs a reusable bow acquisition and replacement policy; forage and dowse need terrain-aware success, retry, and inventory policies.

smithy.strategy: Exploit counterbalance as the first offensive crafting payoff because it permanently gives a weapon an extra-attack chance equal to the learned skill, while avoiding material-heavy upgrades during early leveling.
smithy.practice_policy: With a source-identified wielded weapon, reach weaponsmithing 10%, take one counterbalance lesson, apply it at the Midgaard smithy anvil, then train weaponchain and hurl only after a replaceable weapon and steel reserve are source-confirmed; keep shield block in the defensive rotation.
automation_gaps: The hurl controller and chained-weapon evidence are source-gated; bounded steel acquisition, weaponchain preparation, shieldchain, and material valuation still need live-safe policies.
